messages.author: 364b34b2b0ded261
messages.subject: Phylogenetic 2B-PLS analysis
parts:
Hi all,

I want to perform a 2B-PLS analysis in a phylogenetic context, using the function "phylo.integration". It may sound like a stupid question, but I was wondering in what data format the phylogenetic tree should be uploaded (.nex, .text, .tre, ...)?

Thanks!

All the best,
Marie

messages.author: f16866fc42d43e64
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] Phylogenetic 2B-PLS analysis
parts:
Marie,

the function will accept a phylo object as a tree argument. You can upload that from basically any format using functions of the package ape. See read.nexus and read.tree for that.

Hope this helps
Antigoni

messages.subject: Fwd: Privébericht over: [geomorph-r-package] Phylogenetic 2B-PLS analysis
parts:
Marie,

when working in a phylogenetic comparative context you need to work with species averages, yes. 

Group overlap and dispersal can be investigated, using individual observations, prior to that if you wish.

Please direct future communications to the group, rather than personal accounts, as it makes it easier for a wider public to respond, and other users may benefit from these discussions.

Cheers,
Antigoni

Thank you, this is really helpful!

I just have one follow-up question regarding a phylogenetic PCA. I'm investigating shape differences in wrist bones between different primate taxa. I have a large dataset and investigated the shape differences keeping all specimens separately: I mean I did not create an average shape for each species because this could 'mask' subtle shape differences etc.
BUT, when investigating these shape in a phylogenetic context, and thus uploading a phylogenetic tree in the morphospace, I assume I do need to work with species averages? I ask because I'm worried that making a species average (for example I have 17 bonobo specimens in my dataset) will make it difficult to for example make statements about overlap between species, or mask potential outliers, ...

Marie.

messages.author: f16866fc42d43e64
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] Phylogenetic 2B-PLS analysis
parts:
You can use the average shape array for x, to test for phylosig in all shape dimensions (recommendable), or a matrix with only some PCs to test for phylosig in specific components. The second might be less useful. A useful read for these ideas is 

Collyer, M.L., and D.C. Adams. 2021. Phylogenetically aligned component analysis. Methods in Ecology and Evolution. 12:359-372.

Hope this helps
Antigoni
